comp_disc_analysis.notes:
[chunk 1/3] Source is a DEF 14A Compensation Discussion & Analysis — primarily a comp governance document. SIFI-material signals extracted:

1. CAPEX ROI GAP (Severity 3): Amy Hood's operational review explicitly names $88B in FY25 capex tied to "customer demand signals" in Cloud/AI infrastructure. Commercial bookings exceeded $100B in Q4, but the durability of that demand — particularly given OpenAI dependency — is unverified. Azure revenue of $75B+ on $88B capex spend implies capital-intensity is high and rising.

2. CIRCULARITY (Severity 3): Microsoft is simultaneously (a) a major investor in OpenAI, (b) OpenAI's primary cloud compute provider via Azure, and (c) the distributor of OpenAI models via Azure AI Foundry to 80% of Fortune 500. This three-way investor/supplier/distributor loop is explicitly named in the comp narrative. The "same-day" model delivery commitment deepens operational lock-in.

3. EXECUTION RISK (Severity 2): Azure AI Foundry launched in FY25 with 70,000+ enterprise customers and processed 500 trillion tokens — scale ramp is real but the infrastructure buildout ($88B capex, 2+ GW added, 400+ DCs) precedes full revenue realization and depends on multi-model AI supply chain including OpenAI, xAI/Grok, Mistral, DeepSeek, and Black Forest Labs — all private labs without guaranteed supply continuity.

4. Named AI lab model partners on Azure AI Foundry: OpenAI, DeepSeek, Meta (Llama), xAI (Grok), Black Forest Labs, Mistral AI — establishing supplier concentration risk on the model layer.

No off-balance-sheet vehicles, SPVs, or investment disclosures were named in this section. No explicit equity stake amounts disclosed here.
[chunk 2/3] This DEF 14A section covers Microsoft's Compensation Discussion & Analysis, compensation tables, equity plan information, and principal shareholders. The content is entirely standard executive compensation disclosure: PSA/SA equity grants, incentive plan payout calculations, CEO pay ratio, pay-versus-performance tables, nonqualified deferred compensation, severance plan terms, stock ownership requirements, hedging/pledging policy, and principal shareholders (Vanguard 8.95%, BlackRock 7.30%). There are no SIFI-material entities to extract: no named AI lab relationships, no SPVs or off-balance-sheet entities, no capex commitments, no named customer/supplier concentrations, no investments in private companies, no related-party arrangements beyond standard compensation. The performance metrics referenced (Azure revenue growth, Microsoft Cloud, LinkedIn, Xbox, Search/Advertising) are standard business segment disclosures without counterparty specificity. This section contains zero extractable SIFI-material nodes or edges under the stated hard rules.
[chunk 3/3] Source text is a standard Stock Ownership Information table from Microsoft's DEF 14A (proxy statement), describing beneficial ownership of common stock by directors, nominees, and Named Executives as of September 30, 2025. No SIFI-material entities are present: no named business relationships, customer/supplier concentrations, investments, acquisitions, off-balance-sheet arrangements, AI lab relationships, capex commitments, or related-party arrangements of systemic significance. Pure boilerplate proxy/compensation disclosure — skipped per Hard Rule 3.

beneficial_owners.notes:
[chunk 1/4] This beneficial ownership section of Microsoft's DEF 14A contains no SIFI-material entities or relationships beyond boilerplate governance and audit arrangements. The document lists director and executive shareholdings, audit committee operations, and auditor fees. Notable: (1) Reid Hoffman (Greylock Partners) appears as a director but this is disclosed separately; no hidden leverage, circularity, or concentration risk is evident in this section. (2) The auditor relationship with Deloitte (since 1986 IPO) is disclosed and routine. (3) The stock plan section describes standard equity compensation mechanics with no counterparty relationships or off-balance-sheet arrangements. (4) No private AI labs, SPVs, capex commitments, or investments in AI companies are mentioned in this excerpt. The filing excerpt provided does not contain material SIFI-relevant information beyond standard corporate governance."
[chunk 2/4] EXTRACTION SUMMARY: Microsoft DEF 14A (2025-10-21) — Beneficial Owners section reveals four SIFI-material risk signals tied to AI governance, data ethics, and geopolitical exposure. (1) ESP_Censorship_Risk (severity 2): Microsoft's European Security Program partnerships with EU governments and Europol for AI-powered cybercrime reporting create vague "hate speech" / "harmful content" risk surfaces. Proposal 5 shareholder concern explicitly cites potential censorship weaponization. (2) GenAI_Moderation_Bias (severity 3): Copilot/Azure OpenAI content moderation policies contain undefined, subjective terms ("gender identity," "systemic prejudice") with no disclosed metrics—COST_OPACITY pattern. (3) Recall_Privacy_Execution_Risk (severity 3): Windows Recall screenshot-to-searchable-data feature delayed post-security backlash, then released—execution risk on privacy controls. (4) Saudi_Arabia_Datacenter_HRDD (severity 4, CRITICAL): Datacenter expansion into Saudi Arabia (completed Dec 2024) lacks disclosed human rights due diligence per UN Guiding Principles; State Dept reports Saudi surveillance/censorship capabilities; Microsoft claims Trusted Cloud Principles suffice but provides no enforcement mechanism—reputational + regulatory + operational risk. OpenAI Partnership: While mentioned (extensive partnership, co-development of models), OpenAI appears as separate legal entity managing own data practices; Microsoft discloses arm's-length relationship but inherits reputational/regulatory exposure from OpenAI litigation (NYT copyright suit) and data sourcing allegations. No capex commitments or off-balance SPVs identified in this section. GNI membership provides some third-party assurance on freedom of expression but does not address AI bias or data ethics gaps.
[chunk 3/4] This DEF 14A (2025-10-21) from Microsoft discloses four SIFI-material risk signals: (1) Gaza conflict—Microsoft has confirmed that the Israeli Ministry of Defense violated its ToS via mass surveillance; Covington & Burling performed a review (2) China Uyghur surveillance—Microsoft accelerator program graduates partnered with Xinjiang police (3) Fossil fuel customer concentration—Microsoft controls ~60% of oil & gas cloud contracts; (4) Enabled emissions—just 2 oil & gas contracts have emissions exceeding Microsoft's total Scope 1-3. The filing admits a critical HRDD gap: Microsoft has no visibility into customer use of its software on their own servers. Microsoft commissioned Covington & Burling for third-party reviews but the scope and methodology remain opaque. No new capex commitments or off-balance-sheet entities are disclosed in this narrative section.

It contains NO SIFI-material business relationships, counterparty concentrations, investments in AI labs, off-balance entities, capex commitments, or hidden leverage. The document makes no mention of: (1) customer or supplier dependencies, (2) investments in private companies or AI labs, (3) related-party transactions, (4) off-balance-sheet entities (SPVs, JVs, leases), (5) capex commitments to third parties, (6) circularity or round-tripping. The references to "Parent," "Subsidiary," and merger/acquisition mechanics are standard plan-administration language with no named counterparties.
